source_inspections.author: Barbara E. Mundy
source_inspections.title: La fuente del tianguis de San Juan de México-Tenochtitlan y el segundo acueducto de Chapultepec

source_inspections.author: Kevin Terraciano
source_inspections.title: Narrativas de Tlatelolco sobre la Conquista de México

findings.subject: Indigenous responsibility for aqueduct
findings.assertion: 1591 viceregal order charged two Indigenous alcaldes to protect second Chapultepec aqueduct, paid from caja de comunidad.
findings.exact_locator: p.10, note 8: AGN Indios vol.5 exp.958 f.316 [246]v

findings.subject: San Juan market water access
findings.assertion: Public fountain and paid water distribution required traders in San Juan Moyotlan to carry water approximately an extra 1.5km before the new market fountain; Mundy documents water transport by canoe and mule.
findings.exact_locator: pp.13–14, authorial distance estimate and water-vendor discussion

findings.subject: Inauguration chronologies
findings.assertion: Chimalpahin and Codex Aubin record completion of San Juan aqueduct/fountain in 1582; Chimalpahin gives December 31 whereas Aubin translation has an inconsistent December day.
findings.exact_locator: pp.15–17; Chimalpahin note 31; Aubin fol.63r and note 34
findings.limitation: Conflicting dates; original manuscripts not visually checked

findings.subject: Aqueduct pictography
findings.assertion: Mundy interprets Codex Aubin water signs with white-edged blue bands as plaster-lined aqueduct, unlike unlined navigable canals; year signs connect work to Valeriano government in 1575 and 1582.
findings.limitation: Original pictorial folios not directly inspected

findings.subject: Valeriano and Nahua governance
findings.assertion: Antonio Valeriano governed Indigenous Mexico-Tenochtitlan from 1573 to 1599 and had taught at Colegio de Santa Cruz de Tlatelolco, per Mundy citing 1554 Cervantes de Salazar.

findings.subject: Tlatelolco early colonial fountain
findings.assertion: Sixteenth-century Uppsala city map depicts water reservoir at Tlatelolco market; Codex Tlatelolco year 1555 depicts possible bird fountain; not proven the same fountain.

findings.subject: Tlatelolco manuscript redaction
findings.assertion: Anales de Tlatelolco survives in BNF ms22 on 21 amate leaves and later ms22bis with added or variant material; copy of Rulers List likely seventeenth century.

findings.subject: Cuauhtemoc 1515 disputed
findings.assertion: Tlatelolco Rulers List claims Cuauhtemoc accession 1515, contradicting other Tlatelolco and Florentine Codex accounts naming Itzquauhtzin; treat as contested political memory.
findings.limitation: Do not promote 1515 as historical fact

findings.subject: Temilotzin war and governance
findings.assertion: Florentine Codex XII remembers Temilotzin resisting Spanish-Xochimilca forces with Coyohuehuetzin and wielding captured sword; Book VIII associates him with restoration of Tlatelolco governance.
findings.limitation: Military narrative not independent archaeological proof

findings.subject: Ecatzin captured banner variants
findings.assertion: Florentine XII remembers Ecatzin as Tlatelolca commander; captured-banner mention appears only in later Anales ms22bis, not earlier ms22.
findings.limitation: Later-copy addition not an eyewitness account

findings.subject: Cuauhtemoc execution divergent accounts
findings.assertion: Nahua Rulers List says Cuauhtemoc, Coanacoc and Tetlepanquetza hanged at Acalan without inquiry; Spanish accounts differ on conspiracy and whether two or three leaders executed.
findings.limitation: Conflicting sources; fictional Spain voyage in Rulers List not fact
